poster_title: Ask in Any Modality: A Comprehensive Survey on Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Mohammad Mahdi Abootorabi, Amirhoseiri, Mahdi Dehghani, Mohammadali Mohammadkhani, Bardia Mohammadi, Omid Ghahroodi, Mahdieh Soleymani Baghshah, Ehsaneddin Asgari

panels.headline: Comprehensive review of multimodal RAG systems
content: Covers task formulation, datasets, benchmarks, applications, and key innovations.
Provides a structured taxonomy of state-of-the-art models.
Includes open-access resources and identifies research gaps.

panels.headline: Enhancing LLMs with dynamic external knowledge
content: LLMs have revolutionized NLP but suffer from hallucinations and outdated knowledge.
RAG mitigates these issues by integrating external dynamic information.
Multimodal learning enables systems to integrate and reason over heterogeneous data sources.
Recent advancements in transformers and large-scale datasets have accelerated RAG development.
Cross-modal alignment and reasoning present unique challenges and opportunities.

panels.headline: Pipeline for multimodal RAG
content: Documents are encoded using modality-specific encoders.
A shared semantic space is created for cross-modal alignment.

content: Overview of popular benchmarks used in multimodal RAG research.

panels.headline: Enhancing LLMs with multimodal RAG
content: Multimodal RAG enhances LLM capabilities by integrating dynamic external knowledge across multiple modalities.
The survey provides a foundation for developing more capable and reliable AI systems in this evolving field.
Computational costs and recall degradation remain significant challenges.
Future research should focus on more sophisticated quantization techniques and efficient retrieval methods.
